rows.evidence: Q1: Methods section 2 and Results sections 3.1-3.6 report the authors' own field sampling of drip- and flood-irrigated soils in Hebei, Ningxia and Xinjiang (0-60 cm profiles), ICP-MS/OES heavy metal analyses, ANOVA, Nemerow index and partial correlation analyses.
rows.notes: The study is primary and does compare drip with flood irrigation for heavy metal distribution, but its own result runs opposite to the claimed effect: the abstract, section 3.6 (Supplementary Table S6) and the Conclusions state that drip irrigation had a greater effect on heavy metal content in the soil surface than flood irrigation, the total Nemerow pollution index in the 0-20 cm layer was higher under drip than under flood, Zn reached a 'moderately polluted' level in 0-20 cm only under drip, and the discussion (4.2) says heavy metals often accumulate at or near the surface under drip. The only point in the claim's direction is that under drip the Nemerow index declined more sharply with depth (28.9% vs 9.7%), i.e. drip affects deep layers less, which is not evidence that drip lowers surface accumulation. No wastewater or unconventional water sources were used. Hence no own evidence supporting the claimed effect; Q2 answered no and Q3-Q9 follow.

notes: Full text available including methods, results, discussion and conclusions; supplementary tables (S1-S9) referenced but not included. The study contradicts rather than supports the direction of the cited claim regarding surface heavy metal accumulation under drip irrigation.
